ABSTRACT  
The multiple uncertainties in renewable energy generation and load pose challenges for the operation of inte -
grated energy systems (IES) with robustness. To achieve robust scheduling of IES, this paper proposes a multi- 
objective bi-level confidence gap decision theory robust model (MOCGDT). First, a neural network-based sur -
rogate model is used to obtain the inverse cumulative distribution function of a Gaussian mixture model for 
uncertain parameters, constructing a confidence interval uncertainty set. Then, the upper-level optimization 
objective is to maximize the fluctuations of wind, solar, and load, while the lower-level objective is to minimize 
the total operating cost, resulting in an IES MOCGDT robust model. Finally, an effective bi-level solution algo -
rithm is developed for the model ’ s characteristics. The case study results demonstrate that the proposed method 
improves economic costs by 20.69% and 3.87% compared to robust optimization and stochastic optimization, 
respectively, and reduces computation time by approximately 601 s compared to stochastic optimization. This 
suggests that the proposed MOCGDT model not only reduces the conservatism of conventional robust decision- 
making but also overcomes the coarseness of uncertain sets in the information gap decision theory model, 
achieving more reasonable robust scheduling with uncertainty. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed 
method are thus verified.   
1. Introduction 
With the rapid growth of industries and rising energy needs, the 
efficient and effective utilization and distribution of energy have 
become a significant research focus ( Lawal & Teh, 2023 ). Integrated 
energy systems (IES) have gained significant attention, as they offer 
complementary use of electricity, heating, and cooling energy sources, 
leading to increased energy efficiency and reduced environmental 
pollution ( Li et al., 2023; Zhang et al., 2023 ). An IES is a complex energy 
system with sustainable development, consisting of energy conversion, 
distribution and storage devices, and various end-users. It can provide 
electricity, cooling energy, heating energy, and other loads simulta -
neously. An IES can obtain electrical energy from various distributed 
sources. In addition, cooling energy can be generated by utilizing 
adsorption chillers. To manage the energy supply and demand, any 
excess energy can be stored in electrical or thermal energy storage de -
vices and then utilized during peak demand periods. However, the 
complexity of coupling between multiple energy sources and the un -
certainty associated with renewable energy generation (REG) and load 
demand make it challenging to develop an effective dispatching scheme. 
Therefore, robust scheduling that considers uncertainty is of significant 
importance to the operation of IES ( Mohseni et al., 2022 ). 
Research on the uncertainty optimization scheduling problem has 
been carried out extensively in the last few decades and can be broadly 
classified into two main approaches: stochastic optimization (SO) and 
robust optimization (RO), depending on how uncertainty factors are 
modeled ( Rahmani & Amjady, 2019 ). In SO, the uncertainty is described 
using a probability distribution function (PDF), and typical scenarios are 
generated through sampling. The optimized solution is then the average 
optimal solution across all scenarios. In ( Vahid-Pakdel et al., 2017 ), 
under the uncertainty of wind power output and price, an energy hub 
operation strategy considering demand response and the thermal energy 
market was proposed based on a SO method. In ( Mansouri et al., 2020 ), 
the Monte Carlo method is adopted to generate different scenarios, and 
then the K-means method is used to reduce the scenarios and propose a 
strategy for optimal planning. In ( Zheng et al., 2021 ), the uncertainty of 
load and photovoltaic (PV) production in grid-connected residential PV- 
battery systems is addressed through a proposed two-stage SO method.

distributed generation and the electric vehicle aggregator. In (Tan et al., 
2022), a two-stage RO dispatch model is developed for integrated power 
and heat network. In (Wu et al., 2022), to address heterogeneous un -
certainties in the IES planning of the park, a two-stage RO model is 
proposed to obtain the equipment configuration scheme of each plan -
ning stage. In (Chen et al., 2022), an adjustable two-stage robust energy 
management optimization framework is established considering the 
REG output and load uncertainties. It should be noted that both SO and 
RO have shortcomings: too many scene trees in SO will lead to a sudden 
increase in the amount of calculation, and scene reduction not only loses 
the ergodicity of the uncertain interval but also cannot guarantee 
robustness. If the clustering algorithm is not accurate enough, the 
typical scene after the scene reduction is not representative enough. RO 
is generally based on the preset robustness coefficient for robustness 
analysis, and its robustness setting is often too subjective or 
conservative. 
Information gap decision theory (IGDT) is an efficient model for 
managing uncertain risks that involves analyzing the potential impact of 
uncertain parameters while still meeting predetermined objectives 
(Izadi et al., 2023). In (Mehdizadeh et al., 2018), risk-based energy 
management of renewable energy-based microgrids in the presence of 
peak load management is performed using information gap decision 
theory. In (Vahid-Ghavidel et al., 2019), an IGDT-based robust decision 
model for short-term self-scheduling of demand response (DR) aggre -
gators is proposed, considering the impact of uncertainty in market 
electricity prices and consumer participation on the scheduling strategy. 
In (Liu et al., 2022), a multi-energy retailer scheduling strategy with DR 
based on IGDT is proposed. In (Najafi et al., 2022), a novel optimization 
framework is proposed for optimal self-scheduling of an energy hub, 
which utilizes a combination of IGDT and RO. However, The IGDT 
method is inadequate in dealing with uncertain variables as it does not 
consider their distribution probability characteristics. Moreover, most 
IGDT models only consider the impact of a single uncertain variable and 
fail to fully analyze the relationship between multiple uncertain vari -
ables. This study aims to optimize the dispatch of IES under multiple 
uncertainties, including wind, PV, and load variations, with the objec -
tive of minimizing economic costs. Given the limitations of existing 
optimization models such as RO, SO, and the basic IGDT model for 
handling uncertain optimization problems, a data-driven multi-objec -
tive confidence gap decision theory (MOCGDT) model is proposed to 
solve the IES dispatch problem. Table 1 intuitively summarizes the 
comprehensive comparison between this work and existing research 
work in solving energy management with uncertainty. The main con -
tributions of this study can be summarized as follows:  
(1) To overcome the limitations of the basic IGDT model, which uses 
a symmetric box set to describe uncertain parameters, a Gaussian 
mixture model (GMM) is used to fit the probability distribution of 
the prediction error of the uncertain parameters. An surrogate 
-based model is then used to solve the inverse cumulative dis -
tribution function, which provides confidence intervals for the 
uncertain parameters. The use of confidence intervals instead of 
box sets to describe the range of uncertain parameters improves 
the objectivity and accuracy of the model. 
(2) To address the issue of IGDT’s inability to handle multiple un -
certain parameters simultaneously, the multi-objective optimi -
zation theory is incorporated into the IGDT model, along with the 
confidence interval modeling of uncertain parameters, resulting 
in the MOCGDT robust model for solving multiple uncertain 
optimization problems.  
(3) To validate the effectiveness of the proposed MOCGDT robust 
model, it is applied to IES scheduling problems with wind, PV, 
and load uncertainties. Since the MOCGDT is a bi-level model, an 
efficient bi-level solution algorithm is designed based on the 
characteristics of the model. A multi-objective intelligent opti -
mization algorithm is used to solve the upper-level multi-objec -
tive problem, and the CPLEX solver is used to solve the lower- 
level mixed-integer programming problem. 
The rest of this article will be presented as follows. In Section 2, the 
proposed MOCGDT is described in detail. In Section 3, the MOCGDT- 
based robust model of IES is proposed and the solving algorithm for 
the model is designed. In Section 4, the effectiveness of the proposed 
method is verified on a specific IES case. Finally, the conclusion is given 
in Section 5. 
2. Proposed method 
In this section, we introduce the construction process of the 
MOCGDT in detail. Firstly, the confidence interval of uncertain variables 
is constructed based on GMM in a data-driven way. Then the confidence 
interval is used to replace the box uncertainty set in IGDT. Finally, 
combined with multi-objective optimization technology, the MOCGDT 
model is proposed.

Due to the complexity of the mathematical expressions of the GMM, 
it is difficult to solve its inverse CDF directly. Some scholars fit the CDF 
of GMM by high-order polynomials and then obtain the solution of its 
inverse function by the polynomial root method ( Wang, Shen et al., 
2017 ). However, when the order of the polynomial is greater than 4, it is 
difficult to solve the analytic roots of the polynomial ( Klein, 2003; Serre, 
1979 ). Given this defect, back propagation neural network (BPNN) 
( Wang et al., 2011 ) with good fitting characteristics is used as the sur -
rogate model to directly fit the inverse CDF, and a method to solve the 
inverse CDF surrogate-based model is proposed to avoid the complex 
process of indirectly fitting the CDF and then solving the root of the 
inverse CDF. The reason why the surrogate model can accurately 
describe the inverse CDF of GMM is that the following three conditions 
are met simultaneously:  
(1) The CDF is monotonic, and its inverse CDF is also monotonic, so 
there is a one-to-one mapping relationship between the input and 
output of the constructed proxy model.  
(2) The selected sample points are evenly distributed in the whole 
variable space and the sample size is large enough.  
(3) The surrogate model has a strong fitting ability. 
Since Condition (1) is an inherent property of the CDF, the above 
three conditions can be satisfied only by selecting appropriate samples 
and the surrogate model, and the surrogate model can well fit the 
characteristics of the inverse CDF. Specifically, a large number of sample 
points ( X , Y ) are obtained by integrating the PDF. Note that X represents 
the probability value and Y represents the random variable. Then; X is 
taken as the input and Y as the output, BPNN is used to fit the sample, to 
obtain the inverse CDF. Fig. 3 shows the inverse CDF obtained by the 
BPNN surrogate model when the number of Gaussian components k is 4.

mization model with a multi-objective upper model to maximize the 
fluctuation range of wind-PV-load uncertainties while considering a 
predetermined operating cost, and a mixed-integer lower model to solve 
for the operating cost given a range of fluctuations and confirm it is less 
than the predetermined cost. As per the Eq. (10) , the operating cost of 
IES increases when the wind-PV output is low, and the load demand is 
high. Therefore, the lower optimization model checks whether the 
operating cost meets the predetermined cost when taking the lower limit 
of wind-PV output and the upper limit of load, given a known confidence 
level.

5. Conclusion 
This paper proposes a MOCGDT robust optimal scheduling model for 
IES to address multiple uncertainties. The model aims to maximize the 
fluctuation range of each uncertain variable in the upper level and 
minimize the operating cost in the lower level. An efficient bi-level so -
lution algorithm is developed to solve the model. To overcome the 
limitation of the coarse box set in describing uncertain variables, the 
proposed robust model uses a GMM to construct the confidence fluctu -
ation interval of the REG forecasting error. The model also considers the 
variability of fluctuation magnitude of the same uncertain variable in 
different scheduling periods and the conflict between fluctuations of 
different uncertain variables when the budget cost is fixed. The simu -
lation results show that the scheduling cost of the proposed MOCGDT 
model is 10,207.58 CNY, which is improved by 20.69% and 3.87% 
compared with RO and SO, respectively. The conservatism of MOCGDT 
is reduced and more reasonable. In addition, the computation time of 
MOCGDT is reduced by 601 s compared with SO. Therefore, the pro -
posed model has obvious advantages over RO and SO. Moreover, the 
Pareto frontier obtained by PMOSTA algorithm is better than that ob -
tained by MOAOA, MOGWO, NSGA-II and MOPSO, indicating that 
PMOSTA has the best optimization performance. 
It should be noted that the proposed MOCGDT model in this paper is 
not without limitations. It can be observed that the lower-level model is 
restricted to a single-objective optimization problem. Specifically, when 
considering multiple optimization objectives at the lower level, planners 
may not wish to convert the multi-objective optimization problem into a 
linear weighting problem, but rather seek a Pareto solution set, which 
introduces difficulties in decision-making for the lower-level objectives 
and significantly increases the computational complexity of the model. 
Therefore, in future work, we plan to improve the MOCGDT model and 
apply it to IES planning, multi-regional IES collaborative operation, 
energy storage capacity configuration, and other fields.
